Returns all wire segments, labels, and T-junction locations.","name":"get_net_connectivity"},{"description":"Get the net connected to a specific pin on a component by tracing wires from the pin endpoint.","name":"get_pin_connections"},{"description":"Return just the net name for a specific pin on a component.","name":"get_pin_net_name"},{"description":"Get all nets connected to every pin of a component.","name":"get_component_nets"},{"description":"Get all components (and their pins) connected to a named net.","name":"get_net_components"},{"description":"Trace connectivity from any (X,Y) point — returns the wires, labels, component pins and junction dots at that point, and the net it belongs to. Hierarchical sheet pins and no-connect flags are not reported, so an empty pins_here does not prove a wire dangles.","name":"trace_from_point"},{"description":"Find dangling wire ends, floating labels, and unconnected pin endpoints. Pins, sheet pins, junctions, and no-connect flags all count as connections.","name":"find_orphan_items"},{"description":"Detect accidentally merged nets — distinct net names that KiCad nets together, through a wire path they share or through a name that joins their segments.","name":"find_shorted_nets"},{"description":"Find nets that reach at most one pin — often a missing counterpart, an orphan label, or a stub left by a deleted component. Component pins and hierarchical sheet pins count; a power symbol's own pin names the rail rather than consuming it and does not. Reports the pin and label counts, and every label kind that named the net. Read per sheet: a net a global, hierarchical or power label can carry off this one is flagged cross_sheet_unverified.","name":"find_single_pin_nets"},{"description":"Get all wires, labels, and components connected to a given component reference by tracing net connectivity from each of its pins.","name":"get_connected_items"},{"description":"Find overlapping symbols from their transformed drawing/pin bounds (excluding free text), plus conflicting labels at the same location. Reports any symbol whose embedded geometry could not be resolved and used the origin fallback instead.","name":"check_schematic_overlaps"},{"description":"Export a schematic sheet to an SVG file using kicad-cli. The result doubles as a              machine-readable geometry source: kicad-cli writes every string twice — visibly as              stroke paths, and again as an invisible <text opacity=\"0\"> element carrying x, y,              textLength, font-size and text-anchor — so text content, position and width are              checkable without rendering a pixel.","name":"export_schematic_svg"},{"description":"Render a schematic sheet to PNG: kicad-cli SVG export rasterized in-process (deterministic stroke-font rendering, no system fonts consulted). Returns the PNG path and its actual pixel dimensions; with 'inline' true the response also carries the image as base64 so the caller can inspect its own output. Width is capped at 4096 px.","name":"render_schematic_png"},{"description":"Capture the current render of a schematic sheet as its visual baseline, stored under the project's .konnect/baselines/ keyed by sheet name, with the source file's hash and the renderer identity recorded so a later compare can tell design drift from a stale renderer.","name":"set_visual_baseline"},{"description":"Re-render a sheet at its stored baseline's width and report pixel drift: changed-pixel percentage against a 2% threshold, the changed region's pixel bounding box, and whether the source file changed since the baseline. 'No baseline stored' is an explicit result, not an error; a baseline made by a different renderer version is flagged, never silently trusted.","name":"compare_visual_baseline"},{"description":"Export a schematic sheet to a PDF file using kicad-cli.","name":"export_schematic_pdf"},{"description":"Generate a KiCAD netlist file from the schematic using kicad-cli.","name":"generate_netlist"},{"description":"Return a human-readable JSON summary of the schematic netlist: all components, their nets, pin counts. Nets come from labels and from power symbols. Does not require kicad-cli.","name":"export_netlist_summary"},{"description":"Run the Electrical Rules Check (ERC) on the schematic via kicad-cli and return a list of violations filtered by severity. Violation positions are millimetres on the sheet; the response's `coordinates` object says whether they were corrected for the KiCad versions that report them 100x too small, passed through, or withheld because the KiCad version could not be classified. A report that is not in kicad-cli's ERC shape is an error, never zero violations.","name":"run_erc"},{"description":"Scan the schematic for near-miss wire endpoints (within snap_tolerance of a pin or label but not exactly on it) and snap them into place. Use dry_run to preview fixes without writing.","name":"fix_connectivity"},{"description":"Plan or atomically apply saved schematic hierarchy changes to the live KiCad PCB. Defaults to a non-mutating dry run; apply requires its exact plan revision. Preserves placement, routing, board-only footprints, and footprint artwork. A symbol with no footprint assigned is reported under `unassigned_footprints` and the sync proceeds for every other component. A library footprint that cannot be placed, or a connected pad its footprint does not have, makes the dry run a conflict whose diagnostics name the footprint and every part that needs it.","name":"update_pcb_from_schematic"},{"description":"Place a footprint on the PCB. Uses live KiCAD IPC when reachable; otherwise safely edits a closed board file with revision checks.","name":"place_component"},{"description":"Move a placed footprint to a new X/Y position. Uses live KiCAD IPC when reachable; otherwise safely edits a closed board file with revision checks.","name":"move_component"},{"description":"Set the rotation angle of a placed footprint. Uses live KiCAD IPC when reachable; otherwise safely edits a closed board file with revision checks.","name":"rotate_component"},{"description":"Set X/Y positions and rotations for multiple existing footprints atomically. Uses one live KiCAD IPC update and one undo step when reachable; otherwise safely edits a closed board file once with revision checks.","name":"set_component_placements"},{"description":"Set a placed footprint to F.Cu or B.Cu. When the board is open in KiCad 10.0.6 or newer, this uses KiCad's own native FlipItems IPC command — the same transform the GUI's F key performs, including 3D-model offset/rotation — inside one KiCad undo step. Older or unsupported KiCad reachable over IPC returns an explicit unsupported_capability error rather than falling back to the file. Only when no live KiCad holds this board does it fall back to a guarded closed-board file edit, which flips supported geometry with revision checks and refuses any footprint whose 3D model would need a transform the file path cannot perform.","name":"flip_component"},{"description":"Remove a footprint from the board via KiCAD IPC.","name":"delete_component"},{"description":"Update the value or other properties of a placed footprint via KiCAD IPC.","name":"edit_component"},{"description":"Repair the exact legacy corruption from Konnect issue #244: footprint drawing shapes rewritten as anonymous pads with empty layer sets. Resolves each affected footprint from its library, restores its pads and drawing shapes while preserving placement, identity and pad nets, and applies every requested repair in one KiCad undo commit. Defaults to a non-mutating dry run; apply requires the exact returned plan revision. Requires KiCAD running with the requested board open.","name":"repair_corrupted_footprints"},{"description":"Find a footprint on the board by reference designator and return its position.","name":"find_component"},{"description":"Plan or atomically apply KiCad's Update Footprints from Library operation to placed footprints on the live board. Defaults to a non-mutating dry run; apply requires its exact plan revision. Preserves placed-instance state and pad nets while refreshing supported library-owned content.","name":"update_footprints_from_library"},{"description":"List the graphic items inside a footprint placed on the board — silkscreen, fabrication, and courtyard artwork — with the UUID needed to edit one. Points are footprint-local millimetres, as the .kicad_mod shows them. Each item reports 'editable', plus 'outlines' and 'holes' for polygons: 'points' covers the first outline only, so an item with more than one outline or any holes is reported but cannot be edited here. Requires KiCAD running with the board open.","name":"list_board_footprint_graphics"},{"description":"Replace the vertices of a polygon inside a footprint placed on the board, selected by UUID. Points are footprint-local millimetres, as the .kicad_mod shows them. Use this to bring one placed instance in line with a library change without re-placing the part. Only a single-outline polygon with no holes can be replaced; anything else is refused by name rather than flattened. Requires KiCAD running with the board open.","name":"edit_board_footprint_graphic"},{"description":"Return live board-space pad positions, effective rotations, physical geometry, drills, copper-layer shapes, layers and net assignments for a footprint. Reads the board open in KiCad when it is reachable and falls back to the file only when no live KiCad holds this board — IPC unreachable, or that board not open — 'source' says which, so unsaved placements are visible without a save. A pad's 'net' is its net name, \"\" if the pad carries no net (unconnected), or — reading the file — null if the net node is present but unreadable; treat null as an error, not as an unconnected pad.","name":"get_component_pads"},{"description":"Return the live board-space position, effective rotation, physical geometry, drill, layers and net of a specific pad number on a footprint.","name":"get_pad_position"},{"description":"List all footprints on the board with their positions, layers, and values.","name":"get_component_list"},{"description":"Place multiple copies of a footprint in a grid or line array via KiCAD IPC.","name":"place_component_array"},{"description":"Align multiple footprints along a common X or Y axis via KiCAD IPC.","name":"align_components"},{"description":"Duplicate an existing footprint at a new position via KiCAD IPC.","name":"duplicate_component"},{"description":"Render the board with kicad-cli and return it as a base64 PNG. Note this is              kicad-cli's 3-D board render viewed from the top, not a layer plot -- there is              no layer selection. Use export_svg for layer-aware 2-D output.","name":"get_board_2d_view"},{"description":"Inspect, append, replace, or remove one exact 3D-model entry on a placed footprint. Requires the requested board open in KiCad and uses one native undo transaction; it never rewrites an open board file. Inspect first, then pass its exact models_revision for every mutation. Results come from a fresh live readback.","name":"set_placed_footprint_models"},{"description":"Run the Design Rule Check on the PCB and return structured violation results, with separate error and warning counts in the summary. Prefer this over `get_drc_violations` (pcb_export toolset) — they run the same underlying kicad-cli check, but `run_drc` returns a cleaner breakdown. KiCad runs the complete configured DRC ruleset; kicad-cli has no per-test selector.","name":"run_drc"},{"description":"Set board-level design rules (clearance, trace width, via size) in the sibling KiCAD project file.","name":"set_design_rules"},{"description":"Return the current design rule constraints defined in the sibling KiCAD project file.","name":"get_design_rules"},{"description":"Write the PCB editor Pre-defined Sizes list (track widths and via pad/drill pairs) into the sibling .kicad_pro. These populate the Track/Via dropdowns and W/Shift+W while routing; they are not DRC limits and do not change netclasses. A leading 0 mm track and 0/0 via is always kept as the 'use netclass' sentinel. Pass only the lists you want to replace. KiCad reads the change on next project open. The board file is not modified.","name":"set_predefined_sizes"},{"description":"Return the PCB editor Pre-defined Sizes list from the sibling .kicad_pro: track_widths (mm) and via_dimensions (diameter/drill mm), including the 0 / 0,0 netclass sentinel KiCad keeps at the front of each list.","name":"get_predefined_sizes"},{"description":"Check whether the KiCad GUI application is running and whether IPC responds within a bounded timeout. When IPC does not answer, ipc_failure.kind says why: not_configured, no_listener, access_denied (the operating system refused this account; likely a different account or a restrictive ACL, as with a sandboxed client), handshake_failed (the listener did not complete NNG's handshake, so it is probably not KiCad; this takes NNG's 10 s limit, so pass timeout_seconds above 10 to see it), transport_error, or request_failed (the request did not complete and may have reached the endpoint; an explicit KiCad status such as AS_NOT_READY proves receipt, a timeout or malformed reply does not). ipc_failure is null when no kind was established: the Ping succeeded with AS_OK, or this check's own timeout expired first (timed_out: true).","name":"check_kicad_ui"},{"description":"Launch the KiCAD GUI application and optionally open a project file.","name":"launch_kicad_ui"},{"description":"Copy a routing pattern (traces and vias) from one region of the board to another.","name":"copy_routing_pattern"},{"description":"Set per-layer design constraints (e.g. min trace width, clearance) in the sibling .kicad_dru custom rules file.","name":"set_layer_constraints"},{"description":"Measure spacing between two footprints on the requested board. `mode: anchor` (the compatibility default) returns straight-line placement-anchor distance. `mode: courtyard` returns edge-to-edge distance between transformed, authored courtyard bounding boxes for same-side footprints. It refuses missing or malformed courtyard geometry and does not substitute pads or anchors. Neither mode measures pad, trace or copper clearance; use `run_drc` for electrical clearance and `get_component_pads` for pad geometry. Reads the live KiCad board when open, otherwise the saved file, and reports the source.","name":"check_clearance"},{"description":"Observe the configured KiCad IPC endpoint: running KiCad version, addressable schematic and PCB editors, exact open document identities, and semantic navigation capabilities. Active editor/document/sheet fields are null when KiCad has no stable typed query; open-document order is never treated as active state.","name":"get_editor_state"},{"description":"Read the current selection from one exact KiCad editor, project, document, and schematic sheet instance. Returns stable KIID/UUID identities and refuses stale, ambiguous, cross-project, cross-document, or unsupported selected state instead of retargeting.","name":"get_editor_selection"},{"description":"Deterministically resolve one exact saved KiCad object in an explicitly open project, document, editor, and schematic hierarchy instance. Stable KIID/UUID identity is primary; a human reference is accepted only when it resolves uniquely and ambiguity is returned with candidates.","name":"resolve_navigation_target"},{"description":"Clear, add to, or remove from one exact KiCad editor selection. Every non-clear KIID is first resolved in the explicit saved project/document/sheet, and success is derived only from a fresh exact GetSelection readback.","name":"mutate_editor_selection"},{"description":"Resolve an exact schematic-symbol/PCB-footprint relationship in either direction from stable saved KiCad symbol-path linkage, while proving both explicit live document contexts. This resolve-only operation does not activate or select; pin/pad/net expansion remains unsupported unless a unique stable destination can be modeled.","name":"resolve_cross_probe_target"},{"description":"Add a rectangular board outline of the given dimensions on the Edge.Cuts layer. This appends: on a board that already has an outline it leaves two overlapping rectangles and a DRC failure, so resizing means calling delete_graphics(layer='Edge.Cuts') first.","name":"set_board_size"},{"description":"Return metadata about the PCB: title, revision, company, layer count, paper size, and the number of distinct nets (excluding the unconnected pseudo-net). Reads the board open in KiCad when it is reachable, else the file — 'source' says which. Paper size always comes from the file, and is null when the file cannot be read. A custom (User) size also reports its dimensions in millimetres under 'paper_size_mm' on both paths.","name":"get_board_info"},{"description":"Return the bounding box of all objects on the board (tries KiCAD IPC, falls back to file parse).","name":"get_board_extents"},{"description":"Return the board's enabled layers with their names and types. Reads the board KiCad holds open where it can, so an unsaved stackup change is visible; 'board_source' selects that. A layer's id and its signal/power/user type have no KiCad IPC equivalent and stay file-backed, so 'sources' reports where each part of the answer came from.","name":"get_layer_list"},{"description":"Add a new inner copper or technical layer to the board layer stack.","name":"add_layer"},{"description":"Request an editor active-layer change. The bundled stable KiCad IPC protocol does not expose this editor-session operation, so this tool currently returns unsupported_capability without modifying the board file. It never writes an (active_layer ...) token because KiCad 10 board files do not support one.","name":"set_active_layer"},{"description":"Add a rectangular board outline on Edge.Cuts, optionally using circular rounded corners. This appends: on a board that already has an outline it leaves two overlapping rectangles and a DRC failure, so replacing one means calling delete_graphics(layer='Edge.Cuts') first.","name":"add_board_outline"},{"description":"Delete board graphics — lines, rectangles, arcs, circles, polygons, curves, text, text boxes, and dimensions — that match every filter given. At least one of 'uuids', 'layer', or 'types' is required; 'dry_run' lists what would go without deleting anything, and the UUIDs it reports can be passed straight back as 'uuids'. Footprints, zones, tracks, vias, and graphics belonging to a footprint are never touched, and neither are reference images (KiCad's API cannot identify one). This is how a board outline is resized: add_board_outline and set_board_size append, so calling one twice without deleting the old Edge.Cuts graphics first leaves two overlapping outlines. Acts on the board open in KiCad when it is reachable, else on the file — 'source' says which.","name":"delete_graphics"},{"description":"Add an NPTH mounting hole footprint at the specified position, under the MountingHole library name stock KiCad 10 ships for that drill (3.2 → MountingHole_3.2mm_M3, 3 → MountingHole_3mm). A drill KiCad ships no footprint for is refused. Places KiCad's own library footprint when the library resolves; otherwise an equivalent unplated hole under the same name.","name":"add_mounting_hole"},{"description":"Add a silkscreen or fabrication text string to the board.","name":"add_board_text"},{"description":"Add a copper fill zone polygon on a specified layer and net. Tries KiCAD IPC first — with KiCAD live on this board the zone is created through the API and refilled, so it shows up at once and is undoable there. Only when no live KiCAD answers does it fall back to inserting the (zone …) S-expression into the file, and that result carries a warning, because a file-only edit is invisible to an open pcbnew and is lost on its next save. Refuses a net the board does not declare rather than binding copper to net 0.","name":"add_zone"},{"description":"Import an SVG file as filled silkscreen or copper artwork (a logo, icon, or other graphic). Curved paths are flattened into polygon outlines since KiCAD's board format doesn't support Bezier curves in filled shapes. Tries KiCAD IPC first, falls back to a direct file edit if KiCAD isn't running.","name":"import_svg_logo"},{"description":"Read the physical stackup of the board KiCad holds open: each layer's type, thickness and material, dielectric εr and loss tangent, the copper finish, impedance control, edge settings, and the board thickness KiCad computes from the stack. 'findings' lists unspecified fabrication values and, given 'expected', every value that differs from it. Live only, with no file fallback; read-only, so changes are made in Board Setup.","name":"get_board_stackup"}],"tools_added":73}

tools.description: List all available KiCAD toolsets with descriptions, categories, tool counts, and whether each is currently loaded. Only the starter kit (project, config) is loaded at startup — call load_toolset(name) to expose additional tools in subsequent tools/list responses. Always call this first to discover what tools are available for the task.
tools.name: list_toolboxes

tools.description: Load a toolset by name so its tools appear in tools/list and can be called. Returns the list of tools that were added. Use list_toolboxes() first to see valid names. Pass an array to load several toolsets in one call -- cheaper, one tools/list refresh.

name.description: Toolset name (e.g. 'sch_components', 'pcb_routing'), or an array of names

tools.name: load_toolset

tools.description: Unload a toolset to remove its tools from the active session. Use this to keep the tool list manageable when switching tasks. With auto_load_toolsets enabled, tools reload on use.
tools.name: unload_toolset

tools.description: Return the list of currently loaded toolsets and how many tools each provides.
tools.name: get_active_toolsets

tools.description: Return the most recent tool calls this session (newest first) with call_id, tool name, toolset, duration, status (ok/error/not_found), and error_kind when failed. Use this to self-diagnose — e.g. 'why did the last call fail?' or 'what tools have I been running?'

limit.description: Max number of calls to return (default 20, max 100). Pass 0 for all buffered calls.

tools.name: get_recent_calls

tools.description: Return server uptime, total/error call counts, per-tool statistics, and the path to the JSONL call log. Good for 'what's my error rate today?' and 'which tool has been slowest?'.
tools.name: server_stats

tools.description: Report read-only provenance for the Konnect process serving this call: build version and commit when available, executable path, conservatively detected install source, on-disk binary version, KiCad CLI version, redacted IPC endpoint, proven newer-binary state, platform-specific restart guidance, and whether installed skills, agents, and hooks match this build's bundle.
tools.name: get_installation_info

tools.description: Return the merged configuration (user defaults + project overrides). This is the config Claude should use for all design decisions. 'sources' says where each half came from ('file', 'defaults', or 'not_configured' when there is no project directory). Refuses with invalid_configuration, naming which file, rather than merging defaults in place of a file that cannot be used.
tools.name: get_effective_config

tools.description: Read the physical stackup of the board KiCad holds open: each layer's type, thickness and material, dielectric εr and loss tangent, the copper finish, impedance control, edge settings, and the board thickness KiCad computes from the stack. 'findings' lists unspecified fabrication values and, given 'expected', every value that differs from it. Live only, with no file fallback; read-only, so changes are made in Board Setup.

expected.description: The stackup the fabricator will build, to compare against. Only the fields given are compared.

finish.description: KiCad's finish name, e.g. 'ENIG' or 'HAL lead-free'; compared ignoring case

material.description: Compared ignoring case; for a dielectric, against every sub-layer

name.description: A layer name as this tool reports it: 'F.Cu', 'F.Mask', 'dielectric 1'

thickness_mm.description: A dielectric's is the slot's total over its sub-layers

tools.name: get_board_stackup

tools.description: Get the net connected to a specific pin on a component by tracing wires from the pin endpoint.
tools.name: get_pin_connections

tools.description: Measure spacing between two footprints on the requested board. `mode: anchor` (the compatibility default) returns straight-line placement-anchor distance. `mode: courtyard` returns edge-to-edge distance between transformed, authored courtyard bounding boxes for same-side footprints. It refuses missing or malformed courtyard geometry and does not substitute pads or anchors. Neither mode measures pad, trace or copper clearance; use `run_drc` for electrical clearance and `get_component_pads` for pad geometry. Reads the live KiCad board when open, otherwise the saved file, and reports the source.

mode.description: anchor: placement-origin distance; courtyard: authored courtyard bbox edge distance

tools.name: check_clearance

tools.description: Launch the KiCAD GUI application and optionally open a project file.

wait_ready.description: Wait until KiCAD IPC is responsive before returning

tools.name: launch_kicad_ui

tools.description: Request an editor active-layer change. The bundled stable KiCad IPC protocol does not expose this editor-session operation, so this tool currently returns unsupported_capability without modifying the board file. It never writes an (active_layer ...) token because KiCad 10 board files do not support one.
tools.name: set_active_layer

tools.description: Add a copper fill zone polygon on a specified layer and net. Tries KiCAD IPC first — with KiCAD live on this board the zone is created through the API and refilled, so it shows up at once and is undoable there. Only when no live KiCAD answers does it fall back to inserting the (zone …) S-expression into the file, and that result carries a warning, because a file-only edit is invisible to an open pcbnew and is lost on its next save. Refuses a net the board does not declare rather than binding copper to net 0.

name.description: Optional zone name, as shown in pcbnew's zone properties

pad_connection.description: How the pour attaches to pads on its net

points.description: Polygon vertices as [{x, y}], in mm

priority.description: Higher priority wins where zones overlap

tools.name: add_zone

tools.description: Get all wires, labels, and components connected to a given component reference by tracing net connectivity from each of its pins.
tools.name: get_connected_items

tools.description: List all active design rules (user-level + project-level).
tools.name: list_design_rules

tools.description: Return live board-space pad positions, effective rotations, physical geometry, drills, copper-layer shapes, layers and net assignments for a footprint. Reads the board open in KiCad when it is reachable and falls back to the file only when no live KiCad holds this board — IPC unreachable, or that board not open — 'source' says which, so unsaved placements are visible without a save. A pad's 'net' is its net name, "" if the pad carries no net (unconnected), or — reading the file — null if the net node is present but unreadable; treat null as an error, not as an unconnected pad.
tools.name: get_component_pads

tools.description: Load project-specific configuration from <project_dir>/.konnect/project.json. Project config overrides user config where both exist. 'source' is 'file' or 'defaults' (no file; nothing is written). A file that cannot be parsed or read is refused with invalid_configuration.

project_dir.description: Path to the KiCAD project directory. If omitted, uses the configured project_dir.

tools.name: load_project_config

tools.description: Get all nets connected to every pin of a component.
tools.name: get_component_nets

tools.description: Trace connectivity from any (X,Y) point — returns the wires, labels, component pins and junction dots at that point, and the net it belongs to. Hierarchical sheet pins and no-connect flags are not reported, so an empty pins_here does not prove a wire dangles.
tools.name: trace_from_point

A report that is not in kicad-cli's ERC shape is an error, never zero violations.

output.description: Optional path to write this tool's response as JSON, violations and coordinate provenance together (not KiCad's own ERC report)

tools.name: run_erc

tools.description: Return the current design rule constraints defined in the sibling KiCAD project file.

board.description: Matching .kicad_pcb path currently open in KiCad

expected_plan_revision.description: Required for apply; exact revision returned by the latest dry run

tools.description: Export a schematic sheet to a PDF file using kicad-cli.

all_sheets.description: Include all hierarchical sheets; false exports page 1 only

tools.name: export_schematic_pdf

tools.description: Get all components (and their pins) connected to a named net.
tools.name: get_net_components

tools.description: List all footprints on the board with their positions, layers, and values.

tools.description: Find overlapping symbols from their transformed drawing/pin bounds (excluding free text), plus conflicting labels at the same location. Reports any symbol whose embedded geometry could not be resolved and used the origin fallback instead.

tolerance.description: Coordinate tolerance in mm for label collisions and the origin fallback when library geometry is unavailable

tools.name: check_schematic_overlaps

tools.description: Clear, add to, or remove from one exact KiCad editor selection. Every non-clear KIID is first resolved in the explicit saved project/document/sheet, and success is derived only from a fresh exact GetSelection readback.

object_kiids.description: Empty for clear; one or more stable KIIIDs for add/remove

tools.name: mutate_editor_selection

tools.description: Render a schematic sheet to PNG: kicad-cli SVG export rasterized in-process (deterministic stroke-font rendering, no system fonts consulted). Returns the PNG path and its actual pixel dimensions; with 'inline' true the response also carries the image as base64 so the caller can inspect its own output. Width is capped at 4096 px.

tools.description: Launch the live schematic viewer. The viewer shows the schematic as SVG and auto-refreshes when the file changes. Use this after placing components so the user can see the schematic in real-time as you edit it. For hierarchical designs, pass the root schematic — the viewer discovers every sheet reachable from it and shows a sheet selector.

schematic.description: Path to the root .kicad_sch file to view

tools.name: open_schematic_viewer

tools.name: add_board_text

tools.description: Get all pins and labels connected to a named net.
tools.name: get_net_connections

tools.name: place_component

tools.name: get_pad_position

tools.description: Replace the vertices of a polygon inside a footprint placed on the board, selected by UUID. Points are footprint-local millimetres, as the .kicad_mod shows them. Use this to bring one placed instance in line with a library change without re-placing the part. Only a single-outline polygon with no holes can be replaced; anything else is refused by name rather than flattened. Requires KiCAD running with the board open.

points.description: Replacement vertices in footprint-local millimetres; at least 3.

uuid.description: UUID of the graphic item, from list_board_footprint_graphics

tools.name: edit_board_footprint_graphic

tools.description: Return the PCB editor Pre-defined Sizes list from the sibling .kicad_pro: track_widths (mm) and via_dimensions (diameter/drill mm), including the 0 / 0,0 netclass sentinel KiCad keeps at the front of each list.

board.description: Path to .kicad_pcb file; the sibling .kicad_pro is read

tools.name: get_predefined_sizes

tools.description: Capture the current render of a schematic sheet as its visual baseline, stored under the project's .konnect/baselines/ keyed by sheet name, with the source file's hash and the renderer identity recorded so a later compare can tell design drift from a stale renderer.
tools.name: set_visual_baseline

tools.description: Create a new KiCAD project at the given path. Creates the directory, a blank .kicad_pro file, an empty .kicad_sch schematic, and a blank .kicad_pcb board file. Refuses to replace any existing project file.

path.description: Directory path where the project will be created

tools.name: create_project

tools.description: Return a human-readable JSON summary of the schematic netlist: all components, their nets, pin counts. Nets come from labels and from power symbols. Does not require kicad-cli.
tools.name: export_netlist_summary

tools.description: Load the user's global Konnect preferences. Call this at the start of every session to get preferred manufacturers, fab constraints, default passives, and design rules. 'source' says whether the answer is the user's file or Konnect's defaults (no file existed; the defaults are then written for the user to edit and 'persisted' says whether that worked). A file that exists but cannot be parsed or read is refused with invalid_configuration and is never replaced by defaults.
tools.name: load_user_config

tools.description: Save a project-specific rule or override. Same dot-notation as save_user_config but writes to the project's .konnect/project.json, with the same refusals: an unusable existing file is never overwritten.
tools.name: save_project_config

tools.description: Update the value or other properties of a placed footprint via KiCAD IPC.
tools.name: edit_component

tools.description: Return the bounding box of all objects on the board (tries KiCAD IPC, falls back to file parse).
tools.name: get_board_extents

tools.description: Run the Design Rule Check on the PCB and return structured violation results, with separate error and warning counts in the summary. Prefer this over `get_drc_violations` (pcb_export toolset) — they run the same underlying kicad-cli check, but `run_drc` returns a cleaner breakdown. KiCad runs the complete configured DRC ruleset; kicad-cli has no per-test selector.

limit.description: Maximum number of violations to return

output.description: Optional path to write DRC report JSON

refill_zones.description: Refill before checking: persisted IPC fill with sync_live_board, analysis-only CLI fill otherwise.

sync_live_board.description: Bind the requested open board, optionally refill, save and verify its persisted snapshot before CLI DRC. Finish other mutations first.

tools.name: run_drc

tools.description: Set board-level design rules (clearance, trace width, via size) in the sibling KiCAD project file.

min_via_drill.description: Minimum via drill diameter in mm

min_via_size.description: Minimum via pad diameter in mm

tools.name: set_design_rules

tools.description: List PCB documents open in the running KiCad UI and optionally check whether one specific KiCad project or board is open over IPC.

path.description: Optional path to a .kicad_pro project or .kicad_pcb board to check

tools.name: open_project

tools.description: Check whether the KiCad GUI application is running and whether IPC responds within a bounded timeout. When IPC does not answer, ipc_failure.kind says why: not_configured, no_listener, access_denied (the operating system refused this account; likely a different account or a restrictive ACL, as with a sandboxed client), handshake_failed (the listener did not complete NNG's handshake, so it is probably not KiCad; this takes NNG's 10 s limit, so pass timeout_seconds above 10 to see it), transport_error, or request_failed (the request did not complete and may have reached the endpoint; an explicit KiCad status such as AS_NOT_READY proves receipt, a timeout or malformed reply does not). ipc_failure is null when no kind was established: the Ping succeeded with AS_OK, or this check's own timeout expired first (timed_out: true).

timeout_seconds.description: Timeout for the health check in seconds

tools.name: check_kicad_ui

tools.description: Add a rectangular board outline on Edge.Cuts, optionally using circular rounded corners. This appends: on a board that already has an outline it leaves two overlapping rectangles and a DRC failure, so replacing one means calling delete_graphics(layer='Edge.Cuts') first.

corner_radius.description: Circular corner radius in mm; must not exceed half the shorter side (0 = sharp)

tools.name: add_board_outline

tools.description: Render the board with kicad-cli and return it as a base64 PNG. Note this is              kicad-cli's 3-D board render viewed from the top, not a layer plot -- there is              no layer selection. Use export_svg for layer-aware 2-D output.

height.description: Render height in pixels, clamped to 100-4000

width.description: Render width in pixels, clamped to 100-4000 (kept small since the image lands in LLM context, raise it when detail matters)

tools.name: get_board_2d_view

tools.description: Build the full connectivity graph for a net using union-find. Returns all wire segments, labels, and T-junction locations.
tools.name: get_net_connectivity

tools.description: Write the PCB editor Pre-defined Sizes list (track widths and via pad/drill pairs) into the sibling .kicad_pro. These populate the Track/Via dropdowns and W/Shift+W while routing; they are not DRC limits and do not change netclasses. A leading 0 mm track and 0/0 via is always kept as the 'use netclass' sentinel. Pass only the lists you want to replace. KiCad reads the change on next project open. The board file is not modified.

board.description: Path to .kicad_pcb file; the sibling .kicad_pro is edited

track_widths.description: Track widths in mm for the router dropdown, excluding the 0 mm netclass sentinel (that row is always prepended). An empty array leaves only the sentinel.

via_dimensions.description: Via pad/drill pairs in mm for the router dropdown, excluding the 0/0 netclass sentinel (that row is always prepended). An empty array leaves only the sentinel.

tools.name: set_predefined_sizes

tools.description: Set per-layer design constraints (e.g. min trace width, clearance) in the sibling .kicad_dru custom rules file.

min_clearance.description: Minimum clearance for this layer in mm

min_trace_width.description: Minimum trace width for this layer in mm

tools.name: set_layer_constraints

tools.description: List all wire segments in a schematic with start/end coordinates and UUIDs.
tools.name: list_schematic_wires

tools.description: Move a placed footprint to a new X/Y position. Uses live KiCAD IPC when reachable; otherwise safely edits a closed board file with revision checks.
tools.name: move_component

tools.description: Export a schematic sheet to an SVG file using kicad-cli. The result doubles as a              machine-readable geometry source: kicad-cli writes every string twice — visibly as              stroke paths, and again as an invisible <text opacity="0"> element carrying x, y,              textLength, font-size and text-anchor — so text content, position and width are              checkable without rendering a pixel.

output.description: Output SVG file path (directory used as output dir)

tools.name: export_schematic_svg

tools.description: Scan the schematic for near-miss wire endpoints (within snap_tolerance of a pin or label but not exactly on it) and snap them into place. Use dry_run to preview fixes without writing.
tools.name: fix_connectivity

tools.description: Detect accidentally merged nets — distinct net names that KiCad nets together, through a wire path they share or through a name that joins their segments.
tools.name: find_shorted_nets

tools.description: Generate a KiCAD netlist file from the schematic using kicad-cli.
tools.name: generate_netlist

tools.description: Set the rotation angle of a placed footprint. Uses live KiCAD IPC when reachable; otherwise safely edits a closed board file with revision checks.
tools.name: rotate_component

tools.description: Remove a footprint from the board via KiCAD IPC.
tools.name: delete_component

tools.description: Add an NPTH mounting hole footprint at the specified position, under the MountingHole library name stock KiCad 10 ships for that drill (3.2 → MountingHole_3.2mm_M3, 3 → MountingHole_3mm). A drill KiCad ships no footprint for is refused. Places KiCad's own library footprint when the library resolves; otherwise an equivalent unplated hole under the same name.

drill_diameter.description: Drill diameter in mm. Must be one KiCad 10 ships a MountingHole footprint for: 2, 2.1, 2.2, 2.5, 2.7, 3, 3.2, 3.5, 3.7, 4, 4.3, 4.5, 5, 5.3, 5.5, 6, 6.4, 6.5 or 8.4.

tools.name: add_mounting_hole

tools.description: Return just the net name for a specific pin on a component.
tools.name: get_pin_net_name

tools.description: Find dangling wire ends, floating labels, and unconnected pin endpoints. Pins, sheet pins, junctions, and no-connect flags all count as connections.
tools.name: find_orphan_items

tools.description: Resolve an exact schematic-symbol/PCB-footprint relationship in either direction from stable saved KiCad symbol-path linkage, while proving both explicit live document contexts. This resolve-only operation does not activate or select; pin/pad/net expansion remains unsupported unless a unique stable destination can be modeled.
tools.name: resolve_cross_probe_target

tools.description: List all label instances (net_label, global_label, hierarchical_label) with their positions, net names, and types.
tools.name: list_schematic_labels

tools.description: Re-render a sheet at its stored baseline's width and report pixel drift: changed-pixel percentage against a 2% threshold, the changed region's pixel bounding box, and whether the source file changed since the baseline. 'No baseline stored' is an explicit result, not an error; a baseline made by a different renderer version is flagged, never silently trusted.

inline_diff.description: Also return the current render as base64 for inspection

tools.name: compare_visual_baseline

tools.description: Copy a routing pattern (traces and vias) from one region of the board to another.

net_map.description: Optional mapping from source net names to destination net names

src_x1.description: Source region bounding box min X

src_x2.description: Source region bounding box max X

src_y1.description: Source region bounding box min Y

src_y2.description: Source region bounding box max Y

tools.name: copy_routing_pattern

tools.description: Deterministically resolve one exact saved KiCad object in an explicitly open project, document, editor, and schematic hierarchy instance. Stable KIID/UUID identity is primary; a human reference is accepted only when it resolves uniquely and ambiguity is returned with candidates.

human_reference.description: Fallback reference such as C10; must resolve uniquely

tools.name: resolve_navigation_target

tools.description: Return the board's enabled layers with their names and types. Reads the board KiCad holds open where it can, so an unsaved stackup change is visible; 'board_source' selects that. A layer's id and its signal/power/user type have no KiCad IPC equivalent and stay file-backed, so 'sources' reports where each part of the answer came from.

board_source.description: Which board state to answer about. 'auto' (default) uses the exact board open in KiCad and falls back to the saved file only when it can say why; 'live' fails unless that board is open in a reachable KiCad; 'saved' inspects the last saved file and reports that unsaved editor changes are excluded.

tools.name: get_layer_list

tools.description: Read project metadata from a .kicad_pro file. Returns the project name, schematic and PCB paths, last modified time, project-file format version, and the generator versions recorded by the sibling design files. The compatibility kicad_version is null when those siblings disagree.
tools.name: get_project_info

tools.description: Save the currently open PCB board file via KiCAD IPC. Requires KiCAD to be running with IPC enabled.
tools.name: save_project

tools.description: Place multiple copies of a footprint in a grid or line array via KiCAD IPC.
tools.name: place_component_array

tools.description: List all distinct net names derived from net labels, global labels, and power symbols.
tools.name: list_schematic_nets

tools.description: Observe the configured KiCad IPC endpoint: running KiCad version, addressable schematic and PCB editors, exact open document identities, and semantic navigation capabilities. Active editor/document/sheet fields are null when KiCad has no stable typed query; open-document order is never treated as active state.
tools.name: get_editor_state

tools.description: Return metadata about the PCB: title, revision, company, layer count, paper size, and the number of distinct nets (excluding the unconnected pseudo-net). Reads the board open in KiCad when it is reachable, else the file — 'source' says which. Paper size always comes from the file, and is null when the file cannot be read. A custom (User) size also reports its dimensions in millimetres under 'paper_size_mm' on both paths.
tools.name: get_board_info

tools.description: Import an SVG file as filled silkscreen or copper artwork (a logo, icon, or other graphic). Curved paths are flattened into polygon outlines since KiCAD's board format doesn't support Bezier curves in filled shapes. Tries KiCAD IPC first, falls back to a direct file edit if KiCAD isn't running.

svg.description: Path to the .svg file to import

width_mm.description: Target width in mm (aspect ratio preserved)

x.description: X position of the artwork's top-left corner in mm

y.description: Y position of the artwork's top-left corner in mm

tools.name: import_svg_logo

tools.description: Rename a KiCAD project: renames the .kicad_pro/.kicad_sch/.kicad_pcb/.kicad_prl files and rewrites the internal references that carry the old name. Renaming the files alone is NOT enough — every symbol instance stores (project "name"), and a mismatch there makes KiCAD treat the design as unannotated, losing every reference designator. Equivalent to eeschema's File > Save As. Use dry_run first.

dry_run.description: Report the planned changes without touching anything. Default false.

rename_directory.description: Also rename the containing folder when it matches the old project name. Default false.

tools.name: rename_project

tools.description: Export the schematic and PCB to PDF as a timestamped snapshot/checkpoint. Useful for saving progress before major edits.

label.description: Optional label to include in the filename

tools.name: snapshot_project

tools.description: Inspect, append, replace, or remove one exact 3D-model entry on a placed footprint. Requires the requested board open in KiCad and uses one native undo transaction; it never rewrites an open board file. Inspect first, then pass its exact models_revision for every mutation. Results come from a fresh live readback.

expected_models_revision.description: Exact revision from inspect; required for append/replace/remove

model.description: Complete replacement model; required for append/replace

model_index.description: Exact zero-based entry index; required for replace/remove

tools.name: set_placed_footprint_models

tools.description: Duplicate an existing footprint at a new position via KiCAD IPC.
tools.name: duplicate_component

tools.description: Delete board graphics — lines, rectangles, arcs, circles, polygons, curves, text, text boxes, and dimensions — that match every filter given. At least one of 'uuids', 'layer', or 'types' is required; 'dry_run' lists what would go without deleting anything, and the UUIDs it reports can be passed straight back as 'uuids'. Footprints, zones, tracks, vias, and graphics belonging to a footprint are never touched, and neither are reference images (KiCad's API cannot identify one). This is how a board outline is resized: add_board_outline and set_board_size append, so calling one twice without deleting the old Edge.Cuts graphics first leaves two overlapping outlines. Acts on the board open in KiCad when it is reachable, else on the file — 'source' says which.

dry_run.description: List the matches without deleting them

tools.name: delete_graphics

tools.description: Add a rectangular board outline of the given dimensions on the Edge.Cuts layer. This appends: on a board that already has an outline it leaves two overlapping rectangles and a DRC failure, so resizing means calling delete_graphics(layer='Edge.Cuts') first.
tools.name: set_board_size

tools.description: Find nets that reach at most one pin — often a missing counterpart, an orphan label, or a stub left by a deleted component. Component pins and hierarchical sheet pins count; a power symbol's own pin names the rail rather than consuming it and does not. Reports the pin and label counts, and every label kind that named the net. Read per sheet: a net a global, hierarchical or power label can carry off this one is flagged cross_sheet_unverified.
tools.name: find_single_pin_nets

tools.description: Repair the exact legacy corruption from Konnect issue #244: footprint drawing shapes rewritten as anonymous pads with empty layer sets. Resolves each affected footprint from its library, restores its pads and drawing shapes while preserving placement, identity and pad nets, and applies every requested repair in one KiCad undo commit. Defaults to a non-mutating dry run; apply requires the exact returned plan revision. Requires KiCAD running with the requested board open.

dry_run.description: Report the repair plan without changing the board.

expected_plan_revision.description: Exact plan_revision returned by a current dry run; required for apply.

references.description: Optional reference-designator allowlist. Omit to scan every footprint.

tools.name: repair_corrupted_footprints

tools.description: Update a user preference. Use dot-notation for nested keys, e.g. 'fab_constraints.fab_house'. Call this when the user says things like 'always use JLCPCB' or 'I prefer 0402 passives'. Every other key is kept, and the response is the file as read back. Refuses with invalid_configuration, writing nothing, when the existing file cannot be parsed or read; a persistence failure is mutation_outcome_uncertain, so read the file before retrying.

key_path.description: Dot-notation path to the config key, e.g. 'fab_constraints.fab_house' or 'default_passives.decoupling_cap'

value.description: New value to set (string, number, array, or object)

tools.name: save_user_config

tools.description: Set X/Y positions and rotations for multiple existing footprints atomically. Uses one live KiCAD IPC update and one undo step when reachable; otherwise safely edits a closed board file once with revision checks.
tools.name: set_component_placements

tools.description: Plan or atomically apply KiCad's Update Footprints from Library operation to placed footprints on the live board. Defaults to a non-mutating dry run; apply requires its exact plan revision. Preserves placed-instance state and pad nets while refreshing supported library-owned content.

board.description: Open .kicad_pcb path whose placed footprints will be refreshed

dry_run.description: Plan and report changes without mutating the board

expected_plan_revision.description: Required for apply; exact revision returned by the reviewed dry run

references.description: Optional exact reference allowlist; omitted means all eligible footprints

tools.name: update_footprints_from_library

tools.description: Add a natural-language design rule that Claude should follow in this project. Examples: 'Always use 100nF X7R for MCU decoupling within 3mm of power pin', 'Route USB D+/D- as 90-ohm differential pair'.

rule.description: The design rule in plain English

scope.description: 'user' (applies to all projects) or 'project' (this project only)

tools.name: add_design_rule

tools.description: List the graphic items inside a footprint placed on the board — silkscreen, fabrication, and courtyard artwork — with the UUID needed to edit one. Points are footprint-local millimetres, as the .kicad_mod shows them. Each item reports 'editable', plus 'outlines' and 'holes' for polygons: 'points' covers the first outline only, so an item with more than one outline or any holes is reported but cannot be edited here. Requires KiCAD running with the board open.

layer.description: Only list items on this layer, e.g. 'F.SilkS' (optional)

tools.name: list_board_footprint_graphics

tools.description: Align multiple footprints along a common X or Y axis via KiCAD IPC.
tools.name: align_components

tools.description: Read the current selection from one exact KiCad editor, project, document, and schematic sheet instance. Returns stable KIID/UUID identities and refuses stale, ambiguous, cross-project, cross-document, or unsupported selected state instead of retargeting.

document_path.description: Exact PCB path; required only for editor=pcb

project_name.description: Exact project name returned by get_editor_state

project_path.description: Exact project path returned by get_editor_state

sheet_instance_path.description: Canonical root-to-leaf sheet KIIIDs; required only for editor=schematic

sheet_path_human_readable.description: Optional display path returned by get_editor_state; not used as identity

tools.name: get_editor_selection

tools.description: Add a new inner copper or technical layer to the board layer stack.
tools.name: add_layer

tools.description: Set a placed footprint to F.Cu or B.Cu. When the board is open in KiCad 10.0.6 or newer, this uses KiCad's own native FlipItems IPC command — the same transform the GUI's F key performs, including 3D-model offset/rotation — inside one KiCad undo step. Older or unsupported KiCad reachable over IPC returns an explicit unsupported_capability error rather than falling back to the file. Only when no live KiCad holds this board does it fall back to a guarded closed-board file edit, which flips supported geometry with revision checks and refuses any footprint whose 3D model would need a transform the file path cannot perform.
tools.name: flip_component
